sections.html:
Christian County is large: 724 square miles, the second-largest in Kentucky by area. Hopkinsville is the seat, and the other cities are Crofton, LaFayette, Oak Grove and Pembroke. The county runs on Central time and belongs to the Clarksville metropolitan area, with Fort Campbell on its southern side.

Housing here leans toward rentals. The 2020 census counted 26,435 households in 29,206 housing units, with 49.9 percent owner-occupied and 50.1 percent renter-occupied. About 9.5 percent of units sat empty, and roughly 71 percent of residents lived in urban areas. Many sellers are therefore landlords, and military moves tied to Fort Campbell can leave little time between an order and a closing.

sections.h2: Who to call for each tax or records task
sections.html:
Most of what a seller needs runs through the county clerk's office at 511 South Main Street in Hopkinsville, open 8:00 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays. The clerk's phone menu sorts the common tasks.

Christian County Clerk phone routing for sellers
What you needNumberNotes
Main clerk line(270) 887-4105Menu extension 3 covers copies of a deed or a plat
Legal records division(270) 887-4109Deeds, mortgages, tax liens and releases filed since 1797
Delinquent tax sale questions(270) 887-4109Same line as the tax sale registration notice
Probate and court records(270) 889-6539Justice Center, not the clerk

Value questions go to the Christian County PVA, and the amount of this year's bill comes from the sheriff's tax office. If you can't find a number, the clerk's main line will direct you. The legal records division keeps deeds back to 1797, which helps when a chain of title crosses several generations of owners.

A landlord still owes the tax while a tenant lives in the unit. Property tax is the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and an unpaid year follows the parcel into any sale. Landlords gain the most from early payment, since 2 percent off on several rentals adds up. If a servicer or property manager pays your bill, confirm each year that the payment actually went through.

Fort Campbell families are zoned to the federal DoDEA schools, while Christian County Public Schools serve most other households. A buyer's school question can affect how fast a house sells, so be ready to answer it for your own address.

The schedule comes from state law. KRS 134.015 allows a 2 percent discount for full payment through November 1, charges the printed amount through December 31, adds 5 percent during January and 10 percent afterward. The sheriff's fees and a clerk commission pile on once a bill transfers to the clerk, and the Department of Revenue's own sample shows a bill growing by about a quarter by that point.

If your house lies inside Hopkinsville, Oak Grove or another city, ask that city whether it bills its own tax and on what dates.

Book a conference with the Christian County PVA while the roll is open for public review. The PVA has to explain how your number was reached, and a phone conference is allowed if you ask.

If you can't reach a deal, deliver a written appeal to the county clerk the workday after the review period ends. A local board meets about a month later and weighs comparable sales, contracts, insurance policies and, for rentals, income and expense statements. Anyone paid to speak for you must be an attorney, accountant, tax consultant, broker, appraiser or your own employee, and must carry your written authority.

  • The board can raise a value as well as lower it, so bring evidence for your number.
  • The state's tax appeals board hears later appeals, but only from owners who first used the county board.
  • Payment on the value you claim stays due while the appeal runs.

The clerk holds one sale a year, in summer, and posts the date and a registration deadline on the county website a few weeks ahead. Call the legal records division at (270) 887-4109 for the current schedule.

A state timetable sits behind it. Unpaid bills transfer to the clerk on April 15, and a county sale has to fall between 90 and 135 days after that transfer. In the meantime the county attorney mails notices and the clerk advertises the list at least 30 days ahead. A buyer who wants more than three bills in the county, or more than five statewide, must register with the Department of Revenue 60 days before the sale.

After April 15 a bill becomes a certificate of delinquency with a lien on the parcel, and interest of 1 percent a month plus clerk and attorney fees get added. Paying before the sale ends the matter. Paying afterward means dealing with the new lien holder.

Owners aged 65 and up, or totally disabled, who live in the home qualify. The state deducts $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 from the assessed value before tax is figured. Apply at the Christian County PVA with proof of age or disability. Disability claims renew each year, except for owners with a service-connected disability and owners with permanent findings from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Before you change how the property is used, such as renting it out or moving, ask the PVA how that affects the exemption.

sections.h2: Selling a Christian County house that owes tax
sections.html:
Collect payoff figures first and price with them in mind. The sheriff's tax office can state a current balance, and the clerk can say whether an earlier year was filed as a delinquency. The title company subtracts both at closing and records the release.

Penalties keep running on the statutory dates, so a quick move can get expensive. A purchaser willing to take the house without repairs can close on your date and clear the tax from your proceeds, which beats catching up in cash while you pack. Before agreeing to a price, ask any buyer to show how the tax payoff and lien release will appear on the closing statement.

If a tenant is living in the house, tell the buyer and the closing agent early. Rent, deposits and the lease terms all need to be handled in the contract, and the tax split should follow the deed date.

faqs.q: What is the county clerk's address in Christian County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The clerk is at 511 South Main Street, Hopkinsville, KY 42240, phone (270) 887-4105, on weekdays between 8:00 am and 4:00 pm. The legal records division is at (270) 887-4109.

faqs.q: When is the Christian County delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: Once a year in summer. The county website posts the date and a registration deadline ahead of time, so call (270) 887-4109 for the current schedule.

faqs.q: What happens to a Christian County tax bill after April 15?
faqs.a: The bill moves from the sheriff to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien attaches to the parcel. Interest of 1 percent a month and clerk and attorney fees are then added.

faqs.q: Do I still owe tax if a renter lives in my Christian County house?
faqs.a: Yes. Property tax is the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, no matter who occupies the house.

faqs.q: Can a Christian County owner past 65 reduce the tax?
faqs.a: Yes, through the homestead exemption, which is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the Christian County PVA and show proof of age.
